failure_reason: Site is not operating as a normal storefront. Every URL tested (homepage https://www.denbypottery.com/ and a category-shaped URL https://www.denbypottery.com/collections/christmas) serves only a static administrator notice, with no navigation, no product grid, and no category links anywhere in the rendered page (verified both via raw HTTP fetch and a live rendered browser load). The notice text: 'Anthony John Wright and Geoffrey Paul Rowley were appointed Joint Administrators of Denby Group Limited ... on 31 March 2026. Denby Retail Limited (In administration) operated this website until 4 June 2026. On 4 June 2026 the operation of this website transferred to Denby Home Pottery Limited (Company Number 17210259) and this website is now operated by Denby Home Pottery Limited.' Despite stating operation transferred to a new entity (Denby Home Pottery Limited) on 4 June 2026, the live site as of this check (2026-09-03) still shows only this legal/transition notice on every route tested, not a working storefront - so no genuine seasonal (or any) PLPs are reachable to extract. This is a newer/updated business-state finding than the prior Pet Care project note (which found the same underlying administration event): the company has since formally transitioned ownership per the site's own notice, but the public-facing site itself has not yet relaunched as an operating store.
notes: robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (Googlebot explicitly allowed; no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web/Claude-User/Claude-SearchBot entries) so Claude-in-Chrome access is not policy-blocked - the blocker is the site's own content state, not a bot restriction. Checked: (1) raw HTTP fetch of homepage HTML - body contains only a full-viewport 'stage__proofing' notice div plus asset-loading script tags, zero collections/ links and zero mentions of christmas/holiday/festive/seasonal anywhere in the source; (2) live rendered page via Claude-in-Chrome on both the homepage and https://www.denbypottery.com/collections/christmas - both render identical notice text with no nav/menu/products. No seasonal categories could be discovered because no category tree is being served at all. Recommend re-checking this SR periodically in case Denby Home Pottery Limited relaunches the storefront. RETRY 2026-09-04: robots.txt re-checked - now shows "we use Shopline as our ecommerce platform" (platform migration confirmed) with Sitemap: https://www.denbypottery.com/sitemap.xml; still no Claude-specific disallow (only *, adsbot-google, Nutch, AhrefsBot, AhrefsSiteAudit, Googlebot allow-all, MJ12bot, Pinterest) so not policy_opt_out. Tried, in order: (1) curl_cffi TLS-impersonation brute-force across chrome124/chrome131/safari17_0 on homepage and /collections/christmas - all return HTTP 200 with a full ~247-250KB Shopline SPA-shell HTML, which at first looked like a breakthrough past the original raw-HTTP block, but the shell itself embeds the identical administrator/transition notice text ("Joint Administrators...Denby Home Pottery Limited") with an empty mega-menu app-code block (<script></script> where the mega-menu bundle should inject) - i.e. getting HTTP 200 did not mean getting real navigation/product content. (2) r.jina.ai reader proxy on /collections/christmas - blocked by r.jina.ai's OWN Cloudflare managed challenge (403 "Just a moment..." interstitial), so this route could not even reach Denby. (3) translate.goog (fr target) on /collections/christmas - reached true origin HTML (confirmed via <base href> pointing at the real URL) but content is the identical notice-only shell, same as curl_cffi. (4) Googlebot user-agent via curl_cffi on /collections/christmas - connection timed out (28) after 20s, no response at all. (5) Locale variant /en-us/collections/christmas via curl_cffi - HTTP 200, identical notice-only shell. (6) Real (non-headless-Chromium) Playwright browser via channel="chrome" (actual installed Google Chrome, not bundled Chromium, to reduce automation-detection surface) navigated to homepage and /collections/christmas with full JS execution and 5-8s settle time: rendered DOM (288KB HTML) and visible body text are STILL only the administrator notice - no nav, no mega-menu content, no product grid; captured network requests during load show only analytics/ad-pixel beacons (Google/Bing/Facebook/Pinterest tags, a Shopline anti-fraud beacon at admin.innovelabs.com) and zero product/collection data-API calls, confirming the app never progresses past the notice gate to fetch real content. (7) sitemap.xml and sitemap_collections_1.xml ARE served (unprotected, 582 collection URLs, several with lastmod dates after the 4 June 2026 ownership transfer, e.g. arc-blue lastmod 2026-06-05) and DO list plausible seasonal-shaped handles - /collections/christmas, christmas-gifts, christmas-decorations, christmas-shop, christmas-offers, halloween-favorites, thanksgiving, thanksgiving-baking/-cooking/-dinnersets/-entertaining/-glassware/-offers, easter-essentials, valentine, lunar-new-year, chinese-new-year, black-friday, seasonal-offers, holiday-gift-guide, diwali-gifts, plus odd color-named "halloween" handles (black-grey-halloween, blue-halloween, green-halloween, neutral-halloween, pink-halloween) that read like leftover/legacy or mis-tagged entries rather than a real Halloween category - but this is stale backend/CDN sitemap data only; every live front-end render of every one of these URLs (raw HTTP, real browser JS, translate.goog) resolves to the same content-less notice page, so none of these can be content-verified as genuine PLPs per the rules (no product grid, no qty, no nav context reachable) - listing them without verification would violate the no-fabrication / genuine-PLP rule. CONCLUSION: this is a genuine site-wide application-level gate (Shopline storeInfo.status:0 in the seed JSON = suspended/closed store), not a bot-detection WAF block - every access tier from raw curl to a full real-Chrome JS-executed session reaches true origin content and that content is uniformly the legal notice with no category tree. Original blocked determination stands; recommend continuing to re-check periodically for relaunch.
